svg.text: E. Confirmation and receipt: the browser never decides the outcome
The only thing the page may send is an order number. There is no status field to forge.
The card form's own verdict is advisory
A decline can reach the bank and come back through the form
as an error, so it is never treated as the answer. The one
exception is a form validation problem, which never left the browser.
The page asks confirm-payment
Body: { order_number }. Nothing else. A forged call degenerates
into asking us to re-check the truth.
Terminal rows answer from the row
succeeded, failed, and abandoned are immutable. A repeat call
returns the same receipt without touching the row or the
processor. Calling five times produces the same final row.
Otherwise: a server-side retrieve with the secret key
Our server asks the processor directly. One shared implementation,
also used by the webhook, so the two callers cannot disagree
about what is true.
The amount check is the last word before "succeeded"
The processor's amount must equal the order total, to the cent,
as an integer comparison. A mismatch is never written as a sale:
the row stays in flight with the reason "amount_mismatch".
What comes back: a sanitized receipt
Server math only. No processor payloads, no card data, nothing personal.
It carries the order number, the status, the item lines, every money line in cents,
the Personal Volume total, a short machine-readable reason, and named
3-D Secure fields when the rail populated them.
The confirmation view is rendered from the receipt, not from the page
The cart is cleared only when the receipt says succeeded. A decline leaves it
exactly as it was.
The tax rate printed on the receipt is DERIVED from the receipt's own numbers,
so it can never disagree with the amount beside it. "8.88 percent, NY", not "5 percent".
Two waiting clocks, never one
Waiting for a processor: every 2 seconds, up to about 20 seconds.
Waiting for a person to read a message from their bank: every 5 seconds for the
first minute, then every 10, up to 10 minutes. Never presented as an error.
Past the window, the button becomes "Check this order again".
The one sentence that is never absent
At every moment the page says either "nothing has been charged" or "this is
confirmed, here is your order number". There is no third, silent state.
The order number is shown from the moment the payment opens, before anything
can go wrong, so a lost shopper always holds the one string that finds their order.
The lookup box, the last line of defence
Any order number can be typed in at any time, and the same server-side check
answers exactly what happened to it, including whether anything was charged.
On success the page also fires record-tax, after the receipt has rendered. That is bookkeeping: a shopper whose money has moved must never wait on it.
Sources: functions/confirm-payment/index.ts, functions/_shared/edge.ts (retrieveAndApplyPaymentTruth, mapHyperswitchStatus), www/shop.html
